findings.description: SupplierUpdate/IngredientUpdate are described as 'same shape' as the Create schemas but the plan does not state whether PUT semantics are full-replace (omitted optional fields reset to null/default) or partial/merge. For fields like `safety_margin_days_override` or `supplier_id` this materially changes behavior (e.g. does omitting `supplier_id` on an edit unmap the ingredient, or leave it unchanged?).
findings.required_action: Before/during implementation, pin down and document full-replace semantics for PUT (standard REST convention, and consistent with 'edit forms are pre-filled from the already-fetched list' in §6, so the client always sends the complete current object) and add a test asserting that an edit which changes only one field does not silently null out sibling fields the form re-submits unchanged.

findings.description: The plan doesn't explicitly state that the new seed-script test uses the same isolated-temp-database pattern as `tests/conftest.py` (`test_engine`/`db_session_factory`) rather than touching a developer's real `app.db`. This is almost certainly the intent (consistent with A6's 'opt-in CLI only, not wired into startup') but isn't spelled out.
findings.required_action: Optional: during implementation, confirm `test_seed_demo_ingredients.py` runs against an isolated temp SQLite file (mirroring `conftest.py`), not the developer's real `app.db`. Does not block PASS.

findings.description: `shelf_life_days IS NULL OR shelf_life_days > 0` disallows a `0`-day shelf life for a perishable ingredient (e.g. 'must be used same day'). Plausibly a real edge case for a kitchen dataset, though not required by any AC and not evidenced as an actual current need.
findings.required_action: None required for this gate. If a same-day-use ingredient turns up in real data, revisit the constraint to `>= 0` in a follow-up story.

carried_risks: SQLite runs without `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` in this repo (unchanged, pre-existing posture from ACRI-66); this plan correctly does not rely on DB-level FK enforcement alone for the supplier-picker constraint and instead adds an explicit service-layer existence check (422 on a nonexistent `supplier_id`) with a documented TOCTOU caveat accepted as low-risk at POC/single-writer scale (A11). Revisit if concurrent multi-user editing is ever introduced.

No Alembic/migration tool exists yet; this story adds two more tables via the same interim `Base.metadata.create_all()` mechanism ACRI-66 already established. Recommend introducing real migrations before further schema-changing stories accumulate.

config/project.yaml's development.require_approved_hld/require_approved_lld/require_architecture_validation flags still read true, unreconciled with DEC-005's repository-wide bypass. Same already-disclosed gap carried from ACRI-66; this plan correctly does not modify project.yaml out of scope.

No optimistic-concurrency/versioning on PUT (last-write-wins) - accepted for this POC's single-kitchen-manager-persona scale per the story's own 'no ongoing updates after initial load' out-of-scope note (A11); revisit if multi-manager concurrent editing becomes a real scenario.

Q1 (no DELETE endpoints; manual add/edit/view only) is accepted as the correct reading of the authorized resolution: no AC in ACRI-61 requires deletion, and the narrower scope is safer and more easily extended later. Q2/Q3 (gap-flag visual/copy treatment, supplier-level safety-margin hint vs. hard flag) are accepted as reasonable author judgment calls for a POC with no pixel-level design source for this exact detail - not blockers, consistent with the same category of gap already left open on ACRI-66's login screen.
